H01-02: Inspection of <meta http-equiv="refresh"> tags and delay duration.
Pass: No meta refresh tag found, or it performs a valid operation without disruption.
Fail: A meta refresh performs an instant redirect, has a delay under 20 seconds, redirects without a manual link, or auto-reloads the page.
2. Parse the content attribute to extract the delay and check for url=.
3. Flag if delay is 0s (instant), < 20s (too short), or >= 20s but missing user control.
4. Flag if no URL is present (auto-reloading current page).
If the redirect is immediate (0 seconds):
- Remove the 0-second meta refresh. Use a server-side redirect or provide a button for user-controlled navigation.
If the redirect delay is between 1 and 19 seconds:
- Increase the delay to at least 20 seconds (WCAG recommendation) or replace it with a manual "Continue" link.
If the redirect delay is >= 20 seconds but lacks a manual link:
- Provide a manual "Continue" link alongside the timed redirect to give users full control.
If the tag auto-reloads the current page (no URL):
- Remove the auto-refresh meta tag. Use AJAX for updates or provide a manual "Refresh" button to prevent disrupting screen readers.
